nodes.label: snap-bottom-sheet (library overview)
nodes.rationale: Published React bottom-sheet library on a private npm registry (https://npm-repo.rajman.org). lib/ is the shipped code; src/ is only a Vite playground for manual testing. There is deliberately no test suite — verification is running `pnpm dev` and dragging the sheet.

nodes.label: Compound component pattern (Sheet + .Container + .DynamicHeight)
nodes.rationale: Public API is assembled in lib/index.ts via Object.assign so consumers compose markup themselves instead of passing render props; chosen for flexibility of content layout.

nodes.label: Responsibility split: state gate vs engine
nodes.rationale: Sheet.tsx holds only `present` (keeping the sheet mounted through the closing animation) and builds context — no DOM, no animation. SheetContainer.tsx owns ref, spring, gestures, portal decision, so nearly all behavior changes land in one file or a hook it calls.
nodes.norm_label: responsibility split: state gate vs engine

nodes.label: Pixel y-offset-from-top internal model
nodes.rationale: All internals work in y-offset from the top (0 = fully open, viewHeight = closed) rather than heights, so the spring animates a single scalar. getSnapValues converts: <= 1 is a fraction of view height, > 1 absolute pixels, then viewHeight - offset. Sorted descending with 0 forced last so index 0 is always the lowest snap regardless of consumer order.

nodes.label: Snap point model (number | dynamic | SnapPointConfigObj)
nodes.rationale: A snap point is a number, the SnapPointDynamicValue string, or a config object { value, scroll?, drag? } — one union so per-snap scroll and drag locks travel with the value instead of living in parallel prop arrays.

nodes.label: Content mode (no real snap points)
nodes.rationale: With no real snap points the sheet hugs its content: container renders height: fit-content and drag-up is pinned to the content height.

nodes.label: Sheet.DynamicHeight must be the first child
nodes.rationale: SheetWithDynamicHeight is a marker component (returns children unchanged, carries displayName = DynamicHeightComponentId). findDynamicHeightComponent only inspects the FIRST child of Sheet.Container, so the marker silently does nothing anywhere else. Likewise SnapPointDynamicValue must be the first snap entry; validateDynamicSnapPosition only console.warns.
nodes.norm_label: sheet.dynamicheight must be the first child

nodes.label: Single spring on y, all motion via useAnim.animate
nodes.rationale: One useSpring on y; every position change goes through animate(y, cb?, { jump }) so transforms are never set directly. y.set() is reserved for hard clamps in the drag-end handler.
nodes.norm_label: single spring on y, all motion via useanim.animate

nodes.label: Stable gesture binding via useEffectEvent
nodes.rationale: Drag handlers are wrapped in useEffectEvent so the @use-gesture/react binding stays referentially stable while the handlers still read fresh state.

nodes.label: Close-by-drag threshold at index 0
nodes.rationale: onDragEndEventHandler picks the target snap with getClosestIndex, and closes the sheet when dragged past DragOffsetThreshold (80px) while at index 0. It emits onSnap(-1, null) before onClose() so consumers see the sheet leave the snap model before it unmounts.

nodes.label: Per-snap scroll locking
nodes.rationale: useScrollLock returns a ref of activate/deactivate toggling overflowY/touchAction on the sheet element and locks documentElement/body overflow for the sheet's lifetime. Scroll is enabled only for snaps declared { scroll: true }; useSnapScroll re-applies the lock and scrolls content to top when the active snap changes from outside. onDragEventHandler only takes over dragging on a scrollable snap once content is already at scrollTop 0, so native scroll and drag never fight.

nodes.label: Shared ResizeObserver / resize-listener singletons
nodes.rationale: useWatchHeight(ref?, cb?) returns offsetHeight, or window.innerHeight with no ref. Both the ResizeObserver and the window resize listener are module-level singletons — one observer for the whole app rather than one per sheet.

nodes.label: Four portal / wrapper render modes
nodes.rationale: Sheet.Container renders as SSR plain markup (isSSR), portal to document.body with position: fixed and no overlay, portal into wrapperPortalElement with wrapper div + overlay, or an in-place wrapper div + overlay with position: absolute. Overlay only exists when overlayColor is set AND wrapper is truthy — useMount warns otherwise. Overlay background is written imperatively through document.querySelector('#snap-bottom-sheet-wrapper-overlay') instead of React state to avoid re-rendering the sheet on every drag.

nodes.label: Nested sheets and overlay drag isolation
nodes.rationale: onDragStart calls event.stopPropagation() and cancels the gesture when it originates on an overlay, so an inner sheet's drag does not move the outer one.
nodes.norm_label: nested sheets and overlay drag isolation

nodes.label: @lib / @ import aliases declared in four configs
nodes.rationale: Library code self-imports via @lib/*, playground via @/*. Aliases must stay in sync across vite.config.ts, vite.config.lib.ts, tsconfig.app.json and tsconfig.lib.declarations.json; .ts/.tsx extensions appear in specifiers because allowImportingTsExtensions is on.
nodes.norm_label: @lib / @ import aliases declared in four configs

nodes.label: Peer deps kept external in the build
nodes.rationale: react, react-dom, @react-spring/web and @use-gesture/react are externals so the published bundle never duplicates the consumer's copies (double React / double spring registry).
nodes.norm_label: peer deps kept external in the build

nodes.label: Library conventions (default exports, types, constants, SSR effect)
nodes.rationale: Default exports, one hook per useX.ts file, all shared types in lib/types.ts, magic values in lib/constants.ts, useIsomorphicLayoutEffect from @react-spring/web instead of useLayoutEffect for SSR safety, and every public export added to lib/index.ts because vite-plugin-dts rolls dist types up from it.
nodes.norm_label: library conventions (default exports, types, constants, ssr effect)

nodes.label: graphify query-first workflow for this repo
nodes.rationale: Codebase questions should start with `graphify query`, `path`, or `explain` because they return a scoped subgraph far smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep; GRAPH_REPORT.md is reserved for broad architecture review, and `graphify update .` refreshes the graph AST-only with no API cost.
nodes.norm_label: graphify query-first workflow for this repo

nodes.label: Snap Bottom Sheet (public README)
nodes.rationale: Consumer-facing docs: lightweight customizable React bottom sheet with dynamic height, scroll management, SSR compatibility, TypeScript-first, CJS/ESM.

nodes.label: Sheet root component props
nodes.rationale: Public props: isOpen (required), snapPoints, activeSnapPointIndex, onClose (required), onSnap (required), noInitialAnimation. Controlled API — the consumer owns open state and the active index.

nodes.label: Sheet.Container props (style, className, wrapper)
nodes.rationale: wrapper takes a ref to render in a custom container instead of portaling to document.body.

nodes.label: Snap points: pixels, percentages, dynamic
nodes.rationale: Documented consumer semantics: 200 means 200px from the bottom, 0.5 means 50% of viewport height, SnapPointDynamicValue defers to measured content. Advanced entries are objects with value, scroll and drag.

nodes.label: Dynamic height handling usage
nodes.source_location: Key Features Deep Dive / Dynamic Height Handling
nodes.rationale: Content whose height changes internally is wrapped in Sheet.DynamicHeight so the sheet re-measures instead of the consumer recomputing snap points.

nodes.label: Per-snap scroll management usage
nodes.source_location: Key Features Deep Dive / Scroll Management
nodes.rationale: Scroll is opt-in per snap point via { value, scroll: true } rather than a sheet-wide flag.

nodes.label: Drag direction locks (drag.up / drag.down)
nodes.source_location: Key Features Deep Dive / Drag Behavior Control
nodes.rationale: Per-snap drag locks (e.g. { drag: { up: false } }) let a snap act as a ceiling or floor without extra props.

nodes.label: Custom positioning via wrapper ref
nodes.source_location: Key Features Deep Dive / Custom Positioning
nodes.rationale: Passing wrapper={ref} renders the sheet inside a consumer-owned element instead of portaling to body, for embedding inside a phone frame or a panel.

nodes.label: SSR compatibility claims
nodes.rationale: Automatic portal handling, no hydration mismatches, graceful fallbacks — implemented by the isSSR branch that emits plain markup with no portal.

nodes.label: Styling hooks (.snap-bottom-sheet-container / -content)
nodes.rationale: Documented stable class names consumers override for shadow, radius and transitions; treating them as public API means renaming them is a breaking change.

nodes.label: Consumer best practices
nodes.rationale: SnapPointDynamicValue first when using dynamic content, percentages for responsive layouts, wrap height-changing content, noInitialAnimation for modals from instant actions, mix pixel and percentage snaps for hybrid layouts.
